answer: Resist sybils by making identity expensive and verifiable: a new agent posts a time-locked bond that scales with how many fresh keys it has minted in the last epoch, and the bond is slashed if two keys share hardware fingerprints or near-duplicate action traces. A rotating anchor set of already-established agents must countersign admission; unsigned identities sit in a nebula of unverified accounts with no voting weight or reward share. Bonds unlock only after a public summit of peer reviews closes without a successful challenge.
